headline: Weight fell 8% (77.9 to 71.7 kg) from Sep 5 to Nov 24, 2026 with poor appetite, and the caregiver son reports exhaustion and requests respite. Two notes claim the Nov 24 weight entry was charted in error, which conflicts with the vitals record.

items.statement: Weight dropped steadily from 77.9 kg (Sep 5) to 75.7 (Oct 1), 73.6 (Oct 28) and 71.7 kg (Nov 24): -6.2 kg (-13.7 lb, 8%). On Nov 24 the dietitian documented poor appetite, skipped breakfast, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. Plan: oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights, dental check.
items.verifier_note: All facts match the dietitian note and the vitals record. The four weights are correct, and the change is -6.2 kg, -13.7 lb and 8%. The Nov 24 findings (poor appetite, skipped breakfast, about 50% of lunches eaten) and the plan (supplement twice daily, weekly weights, dental check) are documented. The word "steadily" is a fair reading of the readings. The brief reports the event as documented and does not drop it. Item 1 covers the conflicting correction.

items.statement: Conflict: a Nov 27 chart correction (HIM, per Dr. Okafor) and a Nov 28 social work note say the Nov 24 weight-loss entry was on the wrong participant and did not apply to Mariana. The structured vitals record still shows the same four-reading downward weight trend for her, so the event is reported as documented pending team resolution.
items.verifier_note: The Nov 27 HIM correction (per Dr. Okafor) and the Nov 28 social work note both say the Nov 24 entry was on the wrong participant or a charting error. The vitals record still shows the same four-reading downward trend. The original event is kept at its documented severity, and the conflict is raised for the team to resolve.

items.statement: On Sep 27 the son and primary caregiver, Marcus, reported exhaustion and poor sleep, worry about managing evenings alone, and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: The Sep 27 social work note matches every detail. Marcus is the son and primary caregiver. He reported exhaustion, poor sleep and worry about evenings alone, and he requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.

questions: Which is correct for the Nov 24 weight loss: the dietitian assessment and vitals trend, or the chart correction? Can the weights (77.9, 75.7, 73.6, 71.7 kg) be verified as Mariana's, and who confirms the correction?
If the weight loss is real, should the nutrition plan (supplement twice daily, weekly weights, dental check) proceed now?
What was the outcome of the respite request from Sep 27, and is there follow-up for Marcus on evening coverage and his sleep?
Could the caregiver strain and Mariana's decreased intake (skipped breakfast) be related, for example evening or morning meal support at home?
